chunks: Safwan from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a woman who was with a group of people, so she experienced menstruation. So she sent a message to them and asked them. So they said, 'We do not know if Ihram is upon you or not, while you are menstruating.' So they left her until she entered the Haram. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If there was sufficient time for her, let her return to the time (of Dhu al-Qadah) and enter Ihram from it; and if there was not sufficient time for her, let her return to whatever she is able to do after exiting the Haram, by a measure that does not cause her to miss it (the Hajj).'

key_terms.إِحْرَامٌ: Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman who enters Ihram while menstruating?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides a nuanced ruling for a woman who enters the Haram while menstruating, distinguishing between those with sufficient time to return to the Mi'qat and those without. This highlights the Shia juristic principle of balancing ritual purity requirements with the preservation of Hajj obligations, ensuring the pilgrim is not deprived of the pilgrimage due to temporary impurity. The hadith underscores the flexibility in Islamic law to accommodate natural biological states without invalidating the core religious duty.
